subject: Infra headcount reallocation & comp-band exception for kernel slots
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ACME Cloud Talent <talent@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: shift 4 infra slots from edge -> kernel (comp-band implications)

Team —

Quick summary: after the last planning sync we ran the capacity projections for H3 and found two kernel-focused infra roles (kernel-sre) are now critical to the compilation/kernels roadmap. We can repurpose four open infra slots currently reserved for Edge SRE into Kernel-specific slots with staggered start dates (one Q3, three Q4).

Why this matters: the kernel work has immediate throughput/latency ROI and avoids an expensive contractor band lift we expect if we delay. However, moving these seats triggers a comp-band re-evaluation for two senior-level requisitions: one should be paid at senior-2 band rather than senior-1 to be competitive. That requires a comp exception and confirmation of the budget-neutral trade-offs.

Attached: headcount_plan.xlsx with breakdown, comp_impact.pdf with estimated FY cost delta, and a proposed candidate_slate.

Asks:
- Kim: can you share the payband exception path and whether the finance bucket supports a modest uplift for two roles (approx +12% each)?
- Marcus/Marissa: confirm that the kernel squad can onboard staggered hires (Q3 -> Q4) and that the backlog justifies the prioritization.
- Karthik: any objections on org-routing / long-term headcount distribution?

If we can get a provisional signoff by EOD Monday I can ask Talent to hold the current finalists and adjust offer bands.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform & Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, FinanceOps <finance-ops@partners.redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: shift 4 infra slots from edge -> kernel (comp-band implications)

Jonas — thanks for the write-up and the attachments. I reviewed comp_impact.pdf; high level thoughts:

- The requested +12% uplift on two roles is plausible within our hiring contingency but will require an explicit comp-band exception approval because it crosses the midpoint for senior-1.
- FinanceOps: we need a short memo (1-pager) explaining the ROI assumptions and confirming the uplift is budget-neutral if we decommit the Edge slots this quarter.
- Also, confirm whether any of the candidates in candidate_slate are requesting sign-on or relocation — those are separate line items and will change the effective delta.

Suggested next steps:
1) Marcus to confirm timeline/criticality for kernel milestones.
2) Jonas to provide a one-paragraph ROI memo I can forward to FinanceOps.
3) I will route the comp exception to the comp committee once we have the memo and a confirmed offer structure.

Cc'ing FinanceOps so they can flag any awkward budget windows.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
VP, Infrastructure Finance & Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ACME Cloud Talent <talent@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 14:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: shift 4 infra slots from edge -> kernel (comp-band implications)

Jonas / Kim — brief from the kernel roadmap perspective:

- Confirmed: the kernel release planned for November depends on two senior infra hires to own compilation/kernels deployment and two mid-level hires for instrumentation and CI. If we miss Q3 onboarding for the first senior role, we expect a ~6-8 week delivery slip and additional contractor spend (~$60k) to keep the release timeline.
- Staggered onboarding is fine: 1 senior in Q3, 1 senior + 2 mid in Q4 is our recommended schedule. The squad has capacity for staggered ramping.

Regarding comp bands: I'm supportive of one senior receiving the uplift to senior-2 given market signals. For the second senior, can we structure the offer with an accelerated review (90 days) contingent on performance and comp alignment? That reduces upfront cost and might avoid a full band exception.

Jonas: please send the one-paragraph ROI memo to Kim and cc Marcus. Talent: please hold the two top finalists and note an expected band discussion next week.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, FinanceOps <finance-ops@partners.redwood.com>, ACME Cloud Talent <talent@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: shift 4 infra slots from edge -> kernel (comp-band implications)

Team — thanks for the inputs and the ROI note Jonas provided.

Decision: Execs provisionally approve the reallocation of four infra slots from Edge to Kernel with the staggered schedule Marcus recommended.

Conditions / actions:
- Kim: route the comp-band exception for one senior (senior-2) to the committee. FinanceOps will treat the uplift as covered by the decommissioned Edge slots — see FinanceOps thread for the ledger entry.
- For the second senior, we will offer senior-1 with a 90-day acceleration review and a guaranteed mid-cycle comp refresh if performance milestones are hit. Talent to prepare that offer template.
- Jonas/Marcus: coordinate a short onboarding plan for the staggered hires and provide the 90-day milestones.
- Talent: hold the two finalists and prepare revised offer letters; candidate_slate.pdf attached for reference.

Once Kim confirms comp routing, this is greenlit and you can proceed with offers.

Hannah
